facts.text: A fail-safe system moves itself to a safe state when something goes wrong; for a moving machine, that state is usually reached by a controlled stop or, when time is short, an emergency stop.
facts.quote: A fail-safe system moves itself to a safe state when something goes wrong, and for a moving machine that safe state is usually reached by a controlled stop or, when time is short, an emergency stop.

facts.text: ISO/TS 21815-2 defines collision-avoidance device messages to the machine: SLOW_DOWN, CONTROLLED-STOP, EMERGENCY-STOP and motion inhibit. EMERGENCY-STOP requests stopping machine motion as rapidly as possible when a collision is imminent.
facts.quote: It defines the messages a collision-avoidance device sends to the machine: SLOW_DOWN, CONTROLLED-STOP, EMERGENCY-STOP (to "stop the machine motion as rapidly as possible" when a collision is imminent) and motion inhibit [Chapters 3, 4].

facts.text: South Africa's mining regulation requires the system to fail to safe without human intervention.
facts.quote: South Africa's mining regulation requires that the system "fail to safe without human intervention"

facts.text: The MOSH industry specification requires fail-to-safe within 500 milliseconds of detecting a critical failure.
facts.quote: the industry specification MOSH requires fail-to-safe within 500 milliseconds of detecting a critical failure

facts.text: The MOSH industry specification requires a lost connection to be detected within 500 milliseconds.
facts.quote: with a lost connection detected within 500 milliseconds

facts.text: The MOSH industry specification requires a machine reply within 50 milliseconds.
facts.quote: a lost connection detected within 500 milliseconds and a machine reply within 50 [Chapters 3, 7].

facts.text: Stopping a heavy machine is not always safe: a stop on a slope, under a suspended load, while loading a trailer or ahead of a following machine can cause harm.
facts.quote: A stop on a slope, under a suspended load, while loading a trailer or ahead of a following machine can cause harm.

facts.text: The booklet found no source addressing how a machine can fail safe without causing a stop on a slope.
facts.quote: how a machine fails safe without causing a stop on a slope is not addressed in the sources it found [Chapter 4]

facts.text: Treating sensing degraded by dust or snow as a fault trades directly against machine availability.
facts.quote: treating degraded sensing in dust or snow as a fault trades directly against availability [Chapter 3]

facts.text: Post-braking behavior needs its own hazard analysis, including whether the brake stays latched and whether the machine can roll when the brake is released.
facts.quote: What happens after the brake (whether it stays latched, whether the machine can roll when released) needs its own hazard analysis [Chapters 4, 8].

facts.text: The “unsafe or unnecessary intervention” safety function exists because braking is the fail-safe action but can itself be a hazard.
facts.quote: The "unsafe or unnecessary intervention" safety function exists because the brake is the fail-safe action and may itself be the hazard [Chapter 3]

facts.text: Defining the appropriate safe state for each situation is design work that testing cannot replace.
facts.quote: defining the right safe state for each situation is design work that testing cannot replace.
